Q: Are mysql_real_escape_string(trim($data)) or htmlspecialchars($data) suitable for sanitizing data bound for the database? A:

  1. In general, use filter_var()

  2. In cases where only very specific formats or values are allowed it may be better to use regexes or in_array() of valid values.

  3. Remember that "input" means any source of input that you don't directly control.

  4. If the input is going into a query, use prepared statements (e.g., mysqli)

Q: Setting value on dropdownlist with Razor on ASP.NET 4.8 A:

The issue is likely a data type mismatch or a misunderstanding of how Html.DropDownListFor handles selection in ASP.NET

For DropDownListFor to automatically select an item, the property in your first argument (m => m.SelectedCode) must evaluate to a primitive value type (like string or int) that exactly matches the .Value property inside your selection list. If SelectedCode is a complex object ( As your code its a type of Code class), the model binder will fail to match it, and it will default to the first item.

The Fix

You need to explicitly map your options to a SelectList and ensure your target property holds the primitive ID/Value:

@Html.DropDownListFor(
    m => m.Details[i].SelectedCode, // Must be a string or int ID matching the value below
    new SelectList(Model.CodesToSelect, "CodeIdProperty", "CodeDisplayProperty"), 
    "--- Select ---", 
    new { @class = "form-control" }
) 
//Replace "CodeIdProperty" with the actual ID property name of the objects in your CodesToSelect collection, and "CodeDisplayProperty" with the property you want users to see.

Q: How to append to a file with fstream fstream::app flag seems not to work A:

fstream::app|fstream::out instead of fstream::app. app doesn't make sense without specifying out (one could think it should have implied out, but it doesn't).

Q: getting rank of a user among all users in table A:

I'm answering this because @Hogan claims that to have a general approach. There is a general approach that works on all SQL databases, and that is not it.

The general approach requires a SELF JOIN:

select t.useremail, t.views, count(*) as rownumber
from t left join
     t tless
     on t.useremail = tless.useremail and
        t.views >= tless.views
group by t.useremail, t.views

If you have duplicates on the views, then the following is the equivalent of a dense ranking:

select t.useremail, t.views, count(distinct tless.views) as denserank
from t left join
     t tless
     on t.useremail = tless.useremail and
        t.views >= tless.views
group by t.useremail, t.views

And, since the query does not explicitly mention the database, in most databases, you can simply use:

select t.usermail, t.views, row_number() over (partition by usermail order by views)
from t

Q: Frontend vs. Backend for simple unit conversion logic (UX & Security best practices)? A:

If you don't intend to process the result any further, and this is really only about displaying the converted value to the user, then doing it fully client-side is fine.

Would be a different issue, if you were to send the result elsewhere, and use it as basis for further calculations. You would not want to let a user buying a product in a web store manipulate your converted value, and then use that as base for your price calculation later when the user submits their order.
